Lessons.Title: Equivalent Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Original IM2021 Grade4 Unit2 Lesson7 Equivalent Fractions. Teacher original prep and lesson and student three-page PDF were reviewed; source page2 fraction bars and number lines visually examined. Original Edulytics introduction, title and goal retained. Mathematical representation, not automatic numerical multiplication alone, is the lesson goal.
Warm-up True or False Equivalence (10min): 4/8=7/8 false;3/4=6/8 true;2/6=2/8 false;6/3=4/2 true. Give precise visual, benchmark or part-size reasoning.

Activity7.1 Two or More Fractions (20min): original four shaded bars p2 a2/8=1/4,b2/6=1/3,c2/10=1/5,d8/12=2/3. For each find at least TWO equivalent fractional labels; split given parts into smaller equal pieces or bundle groups. The original number line points are a2/5,b3/4,c6/5,d5/4: describe each point with at least TWO different fractions. Crucially c/d are GREATER than1, not normalised into a capped single bar. On original line c or d choose a new tick location and explain two equivalent names. Teacher reviews source line drawing and freely chosen point.

Activity7.2 Equivalent for Sure (15min): Partner A receives3/2 and10/6; Partner B receives4/3 and14/10. Generate two equivalent fractions for EACH and explain by one valid model. Example equivalences: 3/2=6/4=9/6;10/6=5/3=20/12;4/3=8/6=12/9;14/10=7/5=28/20. Partners question and critique rather than copying numbers.

Lesson synthesis (10min): peer gallery with at least four displays from both partners. Compare different diagrams, partitioning, grouping and number lines with mathematical explanations; numerical Practice is supplementary and cannot grade physical representations.

Independent Edulytics five-minute Cool-down (NOT educator-gated publisher original): model3/2=6/4=9/6 on a consistent one-whole scale and explain why all three name the same point. Teacher reviews diagram and written explanation; exact equivalence question families are already implemented.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent fractions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Different fractional labels for the same part of a fixed whole or same number-line point.
KeyConcepts.Rule: a/b=(ka)/(kb) for any positive integer k.

KeyConcepts.Title: Subdivision and grouping
KeyConcepts.Definition: Break equal parts into smaller parts, or group smaller unit parts into larger equivalent ones.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Multiply or divide numerator and denominator by common nonzero factor.

KeyConcepts.Title: Beyond one whole
KeyConcepts.Definition: The value of an improper fraction may exceed1.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Preserve same whole scale and count parts beyond1.

WorkedExamples.Title: Shaded bar equivalence
WorkedExamples.Question: Name more than one fraction for source part b.
Steps: Original bar has6 equal regions and2 shaded:2/6.
Bundle two adjacent sixths into thirds:1/3.
Divide each sixth into two to get4/12.
WorkedExamples.Check: All same shaded share of one whole.

WorkedExamples.Title: Point beyond one
WorkedExamples.Question: Name equivalent labels for the point on source line d.
Steps: The marked point is5 quarters from0.
Divide quarters into three twelfths or four sixteenths.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent exact fraction reasoning
WorkedExamples.Question: Show why 5/3 and 10/6 are the same number beyond one whole.
WorkedExamples.Method: Convert to equivalent equal-sized fractional parts and check the comparison.
Steps: Multiply numerator and denominator of 5/3 by two.
Both are 1 2/3, so both points lie beyond one.
WorkedExamples.Check: First-party mathematical calculation; original pupil diagrams and open reasoning require separate teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Changing numerator and denominator by different factors.
Treating beyond-one source points as within0..1.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original source c/d number lines go beyond1.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep equal whole scale when labels6/5 or5/4 exceed one.

SummaryPoints: Original teacher warm-up four true/false fraction equations verified.
Original source page2 four shaded diagram values and four number-line point values visually checked, including >1.
Original page3 partnerA3/2,10/6; partnerB4/3,14/10; give two equivalents each and a drawing/reason.
A new tick point on source c or d can have multiple valid answers; peer gallery is teacher reviewed.
